name: Rashidun Caliphate
summary: The first caliphate after the Prophet Muhammad, led by four caliphs. In under thirty years it conquered the Sasanian Empire and most Byzantine lands in the Middle East.

location.value: Arabia, then the Levant, Mesopotamia, Egypt, Iran and parts of North Africa.

terrain.value: Deserts of Arabia, the Fertile Crescent and the Iranian plateau.

resources.value: Farmland of Iraq, Syria and Egypt after the conquests.

disasters.value: The Plague of Amwas (639) killed many in Syria.

urbanisation.value: Founded garrison cities such as Kufa, Basra and Fustat.

migration.value: Arab tribes settled in conquered lands.

economicBase.value: Became the most powerful economic and military force in West Asia and north-east Africa.

tradeRoutes.value: Red Sea and Arabian caravan routes, then Mediterranean and Iraqi trade.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: The dirham; the diwan paid soldiers from taxes.

inequality.value: Arab Muslims, then converts, then non-Muslims.

governmentType.value: A consultative caliphate; caliphs were chosen by a small council (shura) or nominated.

succession.value: Consultation or nomination; three of four caliphs were killed.

institutions.value: The diwan (army register) and the Islamic calendar (introduced under Umar).

eliteConflict.value: The murder of Uthman led to the First Fitna.

armyAndTech.value: Fast-moving Arab cavalry and camel-mounted troops.

majorWars.value: The Ridda Wars; Yarmouk (636) and Qadisiyyah (636) against Byzantium and Persia.

openness.value: Allowed Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians to keep their faith in return for a tax.

religion.value: Islam as the state religion; Christians, Jews and Zoroastrians kept their faiths as protected peoples.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Rashidun Caliphate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)

languageWriting.value: Arabic, which became the language of religion and later administration.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Rashidun Caliphate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)

artsArchitecture.value: Early mosques, such as the first mosques of Kufa and Basra.

sharedIdentity.value: Islam and loyalty to the caliph as Muhammad’s successor.

ideasReligions.value: Spread Islam across the Middle East.

colonisation.value: Founded garrison towns (amsar) such as Kufa, Basra and Fustat.

riseSignals.value: Unification of Arabia after Muhammad’s death.

peakPeriod.value: Under Umar (634–644), when most conquests were made.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Rashidun Caliphate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)

declineSignals.value: The murder of Uthman (656) and the First Fitna civil war.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Rashidun Caliphate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Kennedy, The Great Arab Conquests (2007)

outcome.value: Ali was assassinated in 661; Mu‘awiya founded the Umayyad Caliphate.

sources.value: Early Islamic histories. Checked against Wikipedia (“Rashidun Caliphate”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Sunni and Shia traditions view this period differently.

knownFor.label: Compilation of the Qur’an
knownFor.note: A standard written text under Uthman.
